newsitem.title: USA: USDA April 11 world grain highlights.
newsitem.headline: USDA April 11 world grain highlights.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Friday shaved its estimate for the 1996/97 Argentina soybean crop to 13.25 million tonnes due to dry weather, but left its forecast for Brazil soybean production at 27 million.
In its April world supply/demand report, USDA also lowered its Argentine soybean export forecast to 1.90 million tonnes. Brazil soybean exports were unchanged at 5.20 million tonnes.
USDA raised its forecast for China corn exports to 2.50 million tonnes from 1.00 million estimated in March.

China soybean imports were unchanged at 1.9 million tonnes, but soybean oil imports were lowered to 1.50 million tonnes from 1.55 million. China soybean production was estimated at 13.0 million tonnes, unchanged from last month.

Australia wheat exports were raised for the fourth month in a row to 18.00 million tonnes, while the crop was pegged at 23.50 million, unchanged from last month. Canada wheat exports were raised to 18 million tonnes from 16 million last month.
The forecast for South Africa's 1996/97 corn crop was left unchanged at 8.50 million tonnes, despite dry weather.
World grain crops will total 1,854.66 million tonnes in 1996/97, up from last month's estimate of 1,844.07 million tonnes and above last year's 1,708.37 million.
World wheat was pegged at 581.56 million tonnes, oilseeds at 259.46 million tonnes, coarse grains at 896.20 million, rice at 376.90 million, and cotton at 88.12 million bales.
